name: Tapentadol

tolerance.full: develops with prolonged and repeated use

addictionPotential: Moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: Potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or benzodiazepines
summary: An opioid analgesic drug with potency somewhere between tramadol and morphine, and with a similar action to Tramadol. Also an adrenergic reuptake inhibitor. High addiction potential. Potential for respiratory depression in overdose. Should not be combined with depressants or stimulants.
metabolism: Only about 32% of a single dose reaches the blood, because the liver breaks down a lot of it on the way. In people almost all of it is broken down, around 97% of the dose. The main way is glucuronic acid being joined onto it, and the enzyme that does this is mainly UGT1A6, UGT1A9 and UGT2B7. Some is also turned into N-desmethyl tapentadol (13%) by CYP2C9 and CYP2C19, and into hydroxy tapentadol (2%) by CYP2D6, and those are broken down further in the same way. About 70% of an oral dose comes out in the urine as the joined-up forms (55% as glucuronide and 15% as sulphate), and 3% comes out unchanged.
